How do I use it?
Clicking this will erase everything on screen and start again.

Build mode starts from an empty machine. Going in clears:

  • every solid in the scene — billet, vise, parallels, table, imported models
  • the program in the editor
  • the tool table and the D-offset table
  • the run in progress, back to the first line

    Is there anything to cut yet?
    Start with a lump of metal. You can change its size and material afterwards.

    Want to move the stock itself?
    Pick the thing you want to move, then choose what to do to it. Drag the arrows that appear on it in the view.
    First, what are you moving?
    Now, what do you want to do to it?
    Or drop it straight into the vise
    Want to re-set the origin?
    The origin is the corner the program measures everything from — the machine's X0 Y0 Z0. Pick one of these, then click the spot on the metal in the view.
    Press Esc at any time to stop picking.
    Want to change how it's held?
    The vise grips the metal; the two bars underneath it — the parallels — set how far it stands up out of the jaws.
    Want something else in the scene?
    Ready-made vises, blanks and whole example setups, or a file from your own computer.

    Nothing to cut yet — drop a blank in with one of those, or load a scenario from the Library.

    Showcase
    Material
    The blank re-skins itself a cell at a time — a front crosses it on the diagonal and the new metal follows it across. Machining already done is kept.
    Size (mm)
    Type and the blank resizes as you go — the machining is kept.
    Jaws
    Dovetail
    Machined into the bottom of the blank itself, not parked underneath it — the cutter can reach it and the raymarcher draws it. It runs along the axis you pick, so the jaws close across the other one: ↔ X puts the jaws on Y. Foot is the width across the widest part, at the bottom; the root comes out narrower by the depth times the angle, which is what stops it lifting out. 1.250 × .125 at 45° is the usual prep.
    Solver
    Solve steps
    The cutter takes this away as the program runs. Every surface is a live equation solved per pixel — no voxels, no mesh, exact at any zoom. More solve steps means deeper pockets resolve cleanly; fewer is faster.
    Fixture ▶
    Vise Shown
    No vise in the scene — pick one above, or load a scenario from the Library.
    Parallels Shown
    Auto align re-cuts the pair to the jaws as they stand, sets them flush on both sides and banks one against each jaw face. Bank leaves the bars the size they are and just pushes them home.
    Above the jaws
    Table Shown
    The VF-1 work surface under the vise — 26 × 14, three 5/8 T-slots on 4.92 centers. It arrives with a scenario or with the vise in build mode.

    4 ToolingWhat is in the spindle.
    Cutters are drawn as plain cylinders of the stated diameter. The builder that draws real flutes from a code lives in Tool Models, outside build mode.
    5 Set the jobWhere the metal sits, and where zero is.
    Slide the blank along the jaws
    Flush with that end of the parallels, standing on top of them, jaws closed on the blank's own width.
    Work origin
    The origin is the corner the whole program measures from — the machine's X0 Y0 Z0. Pick what kind of point you want it on, press Set origin, then click that point in the view.
    The grid and the X/Y/Z arrows move onto the point you click, and the program follows — the metal itself does not budge. Shift-click keeps picking, Esc cancels.
    6 SceneExtras and starting again.
    Leaving build mode saves this setup, and the page opens with it from then on — after a refresh, and after closing the tab.

    Toolpath Display
    Focus dim on cursor line
    Show arc centers
    Show full toolpath ahead
    Dim future moves
    When ON, future moves draw at 20% opacity. When OFF, they draw at full brightness.
    Dim future comp moves
    The magenta compensated path follows the switch above by default. Turn this off to keep the whole compensated path at full brightness.
    Rotary Axes (A / B / C)
    Tool moves — the path wraps around a billet that stands still. Part rotates — a trunnion carries the work round under an upright spindle. The choice is built into the toolpath, so changing it re-reads the program and rewinds to the first line.
    Center of Rotation
    What A, B and C swing about, in program units. It tracks the selected part's work origin until you type a value here — then it stays where you put it, and Follow work origin hands it back.
    Linear Axes (X / Y)
    Table moves — what a VF-1 actually does: the saddle carries X and Y under a spindle that only goes up and down. Z always moves the head. Display only; the cut is identical either way.

    Tool Models ▶
    To add the tool to the sim, just insert T# at the beginning, like "T1, 1/2 inch endmill, 4 flute". "T20, touch probe" works the same way — that one measures the part and cuts nothing. Say what it is held in and you get that too: "in an ER16 collet", "shrink fit", "Weldon", "hydraulic", "keyless drill chuck". A tool in a holder is the only kind the changer arm can take a proper hold of.

    Graphics
    Guide

    Hey — here's the short version

    A milling machine carves shapes out of a solid block of metal. It doesn't think; it just follows a list of instructions someone wrote for it. This page pretends to be that machine so you can watch the list happen before anyone runs it for real.

    You can't break anything here. Poke at it.

    Where things are

    • Big dark area in the middle — that's the machine.
    • Strip down the left — that's where you change stuff. Each gray bar is a drawer; click one to open it.
    • Box along the bottom — the instructions themselves. Just text.

    Do this first

    1. Click Program on the left.
    2. Click any card under it — Drill is a good one.
    3. Hit the big yellow ▶ under the view.

    The tool comes down and starts cutting. That's the whole idea.

    Getting around

    • Left-click and drag — slide everything around.
    • Right-click and drag — spin around the part.
    • Shift + right-click and drag — spin around whatever is under the cursor instead.
    • Scroll wheel — closer or farther away.
    • Lost? Fit view — the ⛶ button, bottom left. It always works.

    Moving the view never changes the part. You're just walking around it.

    Those little buttons, bottom left

    They turn things on and off. Lit means you can see it. Hover one and it tells you what it is — and the thing it controls answers back in green so you know you've got the right one.

    Hiding something doesn't delete it. The metal still gets cut.

    Two modes

    There's a switch on the message near the bottom of the view.

    • Sim — for watching. Play, pause, scrub.
    • Model — for arranging. Click a thing to grab it, then drag the arrows.

    If clicking the metal does nothing, you're in Sim. Flip the switch.

    What the colors mean

    The thin lines are where the tool goes. Blue is slow and careful, red is fast, gray is the tool moving through air without cutting.

    When it goes sideways

    • Can't see anything? Fit view — the ⛶ button in the bottom-left stack.
    • Tool waving around in space? The block is parked wrong. Switch to Model and hit Auto align to vise and parallels up top.
    • Want that change back? Undo and Redo sit near the bottom of the view in Model mode.
    • Really made a mess? Settings ▸ Easy ▸ Hold to reset — hold the left mouse button on it for three seconds.
    💡 Everything you do is saved on your own computer, so it's still here tomorrow. Settings ▸ Wipe all clears it if you want a clean slate.

    What it understands

    • Motion — G00 G01 G02 G03, arcs by I/J/K or R, helical when there's a Z on the arc line.
    • Modes — G90/G91, G20/G21, G17, G54–G59, G43.
    • Canned cycles — G81, G82, G83, G84, with G98/G99 and G80.
    • Haas pockets — G12/G13: I first-cut radius, K finish radius, Q stepover.
    • Engraving — G47, I angle, J height, text in parens.
    • 3-axis only (X Y Z); stops and coolant M00 M01 M03/4/5 M07/8/9 M06 M30.

    Heads up: cutter comp isn't applied. G41/G42 parse and the D word lands in Tool Offsets, but the line you see is the programmed path, not the compensated centerline.

    Axes and zero

    Z up, X right, Y away from you. Every setup lands with work zero on the near-left corner of the top face, so X and Y run positive into the material and Z0 is the top. The vise goes in turned a quarter — jaws closing across Y, fixed jaw at the back. Before line one runs, the cutter sits on the origin.

    The drawers

    • Stock — shape, material and size, all live. Change one and the blank re-skins itself a cell at a time and keeps the machining you've already done.
    • Fixture — vise, parallels, table, each with its own show/hide. Auto align parallels re-cuts the pair to the jaws and banks one against each face.
    • Tool Table — every T word found. You supply diameters; arrows step 0.025", typing applies live.
    • Tool Offsets — same deal for D words. Rows appear and vanish with the program.
    • Tool Models — real cutter geometry instead of a cylinder. Load a sample, then call it by its T number.
    • Library — parts, stock, clamps, whole scenarios. Click a row to drop it in; the panel tracks what's loaded.
    • Sim Debug — clock, current move, editor line, cutter tip.

    How the cutting works

    The billet isn't a mesh or a voxel grid — it's an equation. Stock is one signed distance function, every pass adds another, and the part is the first minus the union of the rest, solved per pixel on the GPU:

    part(p) = max( stock(p), −cuts(p) )

    So a pocket wall is exact at any zoom and a 0.001" skim leaves a 0.001" step. Scrubbing back is a truncation — drop the cuts made after that moment and the model is right again. No snapshots, no replay. Needs WebGL2. On High graphics, machined faces come up with a mirror finish.

    Playback

    • Single Block pauses after every line.
    • Speed presets are a real multiplier, so Feed and RPM scale with them and get tagged @2×.
    • The two icons above the presets swap the path between feed-rate color and one color per kind of move.
    • Follow Tool pins the camera to the tip.

    Model mode

    Click a solid to select it. Position, Rotate and Scale are the three buttons beside the show/hide strip — arrows, rings, boxes. Undo and Redo sit above the mode banner and slide the part back rather than snapping it. Select the billet and a bar appears up top with auto-align and left / center / right along the jaws.

    Hiding or showing anything disintegrates it corner to corner.

    Saving

    Program, tool diameters, offsets, tool models and your settings are kept in this browser on this computer. Nothing is uploaded and there's no account. Settings ▸ Wipe all clears the lot.

    ⚙ Editor colors and the hover style are yours to set in Settings ▸ Advanced.
